name: pacmon
description: Dependency notes from .pacmon/DEPENDENCY-NOTES.md, right on your package.json. Document why each dependency exists — plain Markdown, stored in your own repository.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Pacmon only reads and writes documentation files inside the workspace. It never executes code and never accesses the network.

pacmon.decorations.description: End-of-line hint on package.json lines that have a note: 'preview' shows a one-line preview of the note (which layer: see pacmon.inlineSource), 'badge' shows a small marker, 'off' disables it.

enumDescriptions: The first line people wrote; the agent's purpose line when there is none.
The agent's purpose line; the first line people wrote when there is none.
Only what people wrote; a plain marker when the section has none.
Only what agents wrote; a plain marker when the section has no agent block.
pacmon.inlineSource.markdownDescription: Which layer of a note shows next to the dependency in `package.json` and leads its hover. Every note has two layers: the text people write right under `## name`, and the `### Agent notes` block AI agents fill in. The hover always shows both — this picks their order and the one-line preview.

enumDescriptions: A note editor opens in a panel beside package.json — write multi-line Markdown, Ctrl/Cmd+S to save. Unsaved text is kept as a draft when you switch dependencies.
An embedded editor opens right below the dependency line (like Peek Definition), showing the note section — write multi-line Markdown in place, Esc to close, Ctrl+S to save.
Quick single-line capture in an input box; multi-line notes open the file in the active column.
Like input, but multi-line notes open the file in a split BESIDE package.json.
EXPERIMENTAL: dependency lines get a comment-thread UI (multi-line input right on the line, saved to the notes file).
pacmon.noteEntry.description: How notes are entered from package.json.

enumDescriptions: The Pacmon mark just before the package name — filled when the dependency has a note, hollow when it does not — with the words in the hover. Plain click, and the mouse turns into a hand over it.
The package name itself opens its note on Ctrl+click. Adds nothing to the file.
A clickable line above each dependency. Unmissable, and it roughly doubles the apparent height of package.json.
The words spelled out at the end of the line, where they compete with the note preview. Needs Ctrl+click.
A code action, so the lightbulb appears only on the line the cursor is on. Marks nothing at rest, but costs two clicks.

pacmon.noteButtons.markdownDescription: Clickable ways into a dependency's note from `package.json`. Toggle these in the **Pacmon** view in the activity bar. Set to `[]` to remove all of them — the right-click menu and the `Pacmon: Add/Edit Dependency Note` command always work. Note that everything except `lightbulb` marks dependencies that have no note yet, which is the one thing Pacmon otherwise never does.

pacmon.monorepo.description: Which notes file applies to a package.json: the nearest .pacmon/DEPENDENCY-NOTES.md walking up to the workspace root, or only the one at the workspace root.
